input.content:
Six weeks after shipping Skycast 1.0, the numbers taught us more than the launch itself.

We're a team of three that built a 7-day forecast app for Android and iOS. Before 1.0, we ran a two-week beta with 40 users, who surfaced 11 bugs — 9 were fixed before launch. Three things stood out:

1. Small fixes, big reliability wins. Removing a background refresh that ran on low memory dropped our crash rate from 4% of sessions in beta to 0.5% after launch.

2. Cache before network. Caching the last forecast on the device cut app start time from 3.2 seconds to 1.1 seconds.

3. Cut what users don't touch. Hourly radar maps ate a third of design time in the first month, but only 2 of 40 beta users ever opened them. We cut them from 1.0.

Store rating after six weeks: 4.6 from 310 ratings. Top complaint? No widget.

What feature have you cut from a launch that you don't regret?
